title: Testard: general grace offers, particular grace applies
source_text: XXIX. Paulus vero Testardus ante aliquot annos Blaesensis Ecclesiae Pastor in synopsi doctrinae de natura & gratia, thesi 300. distinctionem gratiae in Particularem & Universalem sensu longe diverso usurpat. Nam, inquit, gratia erga peccatores duplex est, Generalis, & Particularis. Generalis quae toti mundo datur, Oblatio & facultas salutis. Particularis quae est Electorum tantum, salutis applicatio. Cujus fundamentum proximum est electio libera: medium vocatio efficax: corona justificatio, custodia, glorificatio. Et statim gratiam illam particularem dicit esse vel praevenientem, qualis est Electio & Vocatio: Vel misericorditer remunerantem, qualis est justificatio, custodia, glorificatio.
pass_a_gloss: XXIX. But Paul Testard some years ago Pastor of the Church of Blois in the synopsis of the doctrine on nature and grace, thesis 300. uses the distinction of grace into Particular and Universal in a far different sense. For, he says, grace toward sinners is twofold, General, and Particular. General which is given to the whole world, the Offer and power of salvation. Particular which is of the Elect only, the application of salvation. Of which the nearest foundation is free election: the middle efficacious calling: the crown justification, keeping, glorification. And straightway he says that particular grace is either prevenient, such as is Election and Calling: Or mercifully rewarding, such as is justification, keeping, glorification.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXIX. Paul Testard, some years ago pastor of the church at Blois, uses the distinction of grace into particular and universal in a very different sense in his synopsis of the doctrine of nature and grace (thesis 300).

Grace toward sinners, he says, is of two kinds, general and particular. General grace is given to the whole world: it is the offer of salvation and the power to be saved. Particular grace belongs to the elect alone: it is the application of salvation. Its nearest foundation is free election, its middle stage effectual calling, and its crown justification, preservation and glorification.
He immediately adds that this particular grace is either prevenient, such as election and calling, or mercifully rewarding, such as justification, preservation and glorification.

lemmas.gloss: uses in a far different sense
the Offer and power of salvation

choices.why: The Reformed pair of the 1630s-1650s debates (Polanus, Testard, Amyraut); kept literal because each author fills the terms differently.
